  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**To:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Re:** Where the Seller's package departs from Buyer's interests, and what to push back on
**Date:** 6 November 2026

## 1. Headline view

The Seller's covering note describes the package as "fair and balanced", but the Disclosure Letter itself contradicts almost every reassuring statement in the Seller Update. Read side by side:

| Seller Update says | Disclosure Letter actually says |
|---|---|
| Bluefen consent "is addressed" | Consent **not** obtained; no evidence 11.3 conditions satisfied |
| Riverlark release "to be provided following Completion" | Facility **not** repaid; no discharge of security |
| Ironquay indemnity "considered adequate" | AUD 180k open; no receipt, no confirmatory assignment |
| Bonuses "a matter for the Seller" | AUD 420k **not** in funds flow; on-costs unknown |
| DD-006 "not expected to be material" | Investigation preliminary; scope and notification obligation unknown |
| Sandbar renewals "ordinary course" | Disclosure doesn't say whether unavoidable, terminable or accrued |

The structural problem is this: the Seller wants (a) everything in the data room to count as "disclosed" (so no warranty claim lies for any of these known issues), and (b) a low cap, short time limit and deemed-knowledge clause for everything else. The result is that the identified problems fall between the cracks – not warranty-claimable because disclosed, and not separately indemnified. We should not accept that architecture.

Rough sizing of the *known* items against a AUD 24m debt-free/cash-free price:

- Riverlark facility: ~AUD 3,200,000 (should come off the price or be repaid from proceeds)
- Closing bonuses: AUD 420,000 plus super/payroll tax/on-costs (likely ~AUD 50–65k more)
- Ironquay SOW3: AUD 180,000 (and, more importantly, product IP ownership)
- Sandbar renewals: AUD 330,000
- Bluefen: ~AUD 3,600,000 p.a. revenue (~30%) at risk if consent fails
- DD-006: unquantified regulatory/claims exposure

That is roughly AUD 4.2m of hard liabilities plus two unquantified risks, against a proposed general cap of AUD 4.8m that these items would not even be able to access.

Note also that the Disclosure Letter is cut off at **22 September 2026** – six weeks ago – and the Seller reserves the right to make no conclusions. We must require bring-down and updated disclosure (see §4.4).

Caveat: I have worked from the Seller's summaries of DD-002 to DD-012, not the underlying documents. Each point below should be checked against the primary documents before we respond.

---

## 2. Liability regime (Clauses 9.3, 12, 13, 20.5, 8.3)

### 2.1 Fundamental/title/capacity warranties subject to general cap and time limits – **reject**

This is the most serious drafting point. Title and capacity warranties are the Buyer's assurance that it actually owns what it paid AUD 24m for. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap them at 20% or lose them after 18 months.

**Position:** Title, capacity and authority warranties capped at 100% of the price (or uncapped), 6–7 year claim period (or the statutory limitation period), not subject to de minimis/basket, and not qualified by disclosure or Buyer knowledge.

### 2.2 "Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" and limitations/exclusive-remedy/non-reliance "apply to all Claims of any nature" – **reject**

These two provisions together would sweep specific indemnities, the tax indemnity, leakage/price-adjustment claims, covenant breaches, and even fraud into the 20%/18-month/basket regime. That defeats the purpose of negotiating specific indemnities at all.

**Position:** Clause 12 limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. Express carve-outs for:
- fraud, dishonesty, wilful concealment (and note a non-reliance clause cannot in any event exclude liability for misleading or deceptive conduct under ACL s 18 – the Seller's drafting overreaches);
- fundamental/title/capacity warranties;
- tax warranties and the tax indemnity;
- all specific indemnities (Riverlark, Ironquay, bonuses, DD-006, and any others agreed);
- completion accounts/price adjustment or leakage claims;
- breach of pre- and post-Completion covenants (conduct of business, restraints, confidentiality).

Exclusive-remedy (12.8) should likewise exclude fraud, specific indemnities, injunctive relief and statutory rights that cannot be excluded.

### 2.3 General cap 20% (AUD 4.8m) – **negotiate up, and make the carve-outs the priority**

20% is at the low end of the Australian mid-market range for a deal without W&I insurance. The known-issue profile here (30% revenue concentration, unresolved IP chain of title, an open privacy incident) justifies a higher cap. Open at 50%, settle around 30–35%, but trade cap percentage for the carve-outs in 2.2 rather than the other way around. If the Seller insists on 20%, ask whether they will fund a W&I policy – noting W&I will exclude every known issue listed above, so specific indemnities remain essential regardless.

### 2.4 De minimis AUD 25,000 / basket AUD 250,000 "excess only" – **push back**

- AUD 25,000 is ~0.1% of price; a de minimis at 0.05% (AUD 10–15k) is more typical. Also require that related claims arising from the same facts aggregate for de minimis purposes.
- The basket is drafted as a true deductible (excess only). Push for a **tipping** basket (first-dollar recovery once AUD 250k is exceeded). At 1% of price the quantum is acceptable; the "excess only" structure is the point to resist.
- Tax, title and specific indemnity claims should not count toward or be subject to either threshold.

### 2.5 18-month claim period – **extend**

Push for 24 months for general warranties so the Buyer has one full audit cycle plus time to notify. Tax: 7 years from Completion (ATO amendment periods, plus unlimited for fraud/evasion). Title: 6–7 years. Also ensure the clause requires only *notification* within the period, with a reasonable further period (e.g. 6–9 months) to commence proceedings, and that a notified claim survives.

### 2.6 Clause 8.3 – deemed Buyer knowledge of anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records – **reject outright**

This clause, combined with general disclosure (§3), would strip the warranties of substantially all value: the Seller could defend any claim by pointing to a document somewhere in the data room, or a public search the Buyer "could" have done. It also makes the warranties worthless to W&I insurers.

**Position:** Delete. Fallback: a claim is excluded only where the matter was *fairly disclosed* in the Disclosure Letter (per §3.1 standard) or was within the *actual* knowledge of a named short list of Buyer deal-team individuals, with no imputation of advisers' knowledge and no constructive knowledge.

---

## 3. Disclosure (Schedule 7 and the Disclosure Letter)

### 3.1 General disclosure of the entire data room and public registers (paras 1.1–1.2) – **reject**

Blanket disclosure of "every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in" the data room is not fair disclosure. It makes the Buyer the insurer of its own diligence.

**Position:**
- Disclosure is effective only if made in the Disclosure Letter with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its likely effect ("fair disclosure" standard).
- Data room disclosure limited to documents specifically referenced against specific warranties, from a frozen, indexed data room on a USB/DVD, initialled by both sides, scheduled to the SPA.
- Public register disclosure limited to named searches (ASIC company search, PPSR, IP Australia, specified court lists) as at a specified date.
- No disclosure against fundamental, title or tax warranties, or against any specific indemnity.

### 3.2 Para 1.4 (no admission that any consent, payment, notice, etc. is required)

Acceptable as a non-admission, but it signals that the Seller will not warrant anything about the legal effect of these documents. We must therefore obtain express warranties that: no consent, notice or waiver is required from any counterparty, landlord or financier as a result of the transaction except as specifically listed; and all such consents listed have been obtained in form reasonably acceptable to the Buyer.

### 3.3 Para 11 (Reservation)

This is a signal that the Seller intends to rely on "you were told the facts; you drew your own conclusions". We counter this by converting each disclosed fact into a condition, completion deliverable, price adjustment or specific indemnity rather than accepting the facts as risk transferred to us.

### 3.4 Disclosure cut-off 22 September 2026 – require updated disclosure with limits

Six weeks have passed, and the DD-006 investigation and Bluefen/Riverlark positions will have moved. Require a bring-down of warranties at Completion. Any supplementary disclosure between signing and Completion should **not** cure breaches for claim purposes, and material new disclosure should give the Buyer a termination right (or price renegotiation).

---

## 4. Specific issues

### 4.1 Bluefen (DD-002) – ~30% of revenue; change-of-control consent not obtained

Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and that the condition is "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent."

Problems: (i) "reasonable endeavours" is the weakest standard; (ii) a written consent that is conditional (on 11.3 conditions, pricing concessions, or a new term) would be deemed to satisfy the condition even if unacceptable to us; (iii) the Seller's Disclosure confirms no evidence the 11.3 conditions can be met.

**Position:**
- Condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer, that Bluefen has given written consent **unconditionally, or on terms acceptable to the Buyer (acting reasonably)**, with all clause 11.3 conditions satisfied or waived, and the consent not having been withdrawn at Completion.
- Seller to use **all reasonable endeavours / best endeavours**, keep the Buyer informed, and allow the Buyer to participate in discussions with Bluefen.
- Warranty that Bluefen has not notified any intention to terminate, reduce volumes or renegotiate pricing.
- If the Seller will not accept the CP: price reduction, or a revenue-based earn-out/deferred consideration tied to Bluefen retention for 12–24 months.
- Given concentration, we also want 11.2/11.3 reviewed ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's summary.

### 4.2 Riverlark Bank (DD-003) – AUD 3.2m facility; release "following Completion" – **reject**

The deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release means the Buyer acquires a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt, a lender entitled to call default under change-of-control clause 8.1 on the day of Completion, and security remaining over the business.

**Position:**
- Facility repaid **at Completion** from the purchase price via the funds flow (payoff letter from Riverlark stating the exact payout figure, with per-diem interest and break costs).
- Completion deliverables: executed deed of release/discharge, release of all guarantees given by the Company or its directors, PPSR financing change statements (or undertaking to lodge within 2 business days with Seller covenant and indemnity for failure).
- Any break costs, early repayment fees or hedging close-out are Seller costs (deducted from price).
- Confirm no other PPSR registrations, guarantees or intercompany debt to Harbourglass; all intercompany balances settled or released at Completion.

### 4.3 Completion bonuses (DD-005) – AUD 420,000, not in funds flow

The Seller says these are "a matter for the Seller", but the payer under the bonus letters is almost certainly the Company. If they fall due post-Completion, the Buyer funds them – a straight AUD 420k+ transfer of value to the Seller in breach of the debt-free/cash-free principle.

**Position:**
- Treat bonuses plus employer superannuation, payroll tax, workers' comp and any other on-costs (plus any leave loading consequences) as **Transaction Expenses / Debt-like items** deducted from the price in the funds flow, or paid by the Seller through the Company pre-Completion with a matching cash top-up.
- Specific indemnity for any bonus, on-cost or employment claim arising from the bonus arrangements.
- Review the "continued-employment" condition: if payment is conditional on post-Completion employment, clarify who bears forfeited/retention risk and ensure the arrangements don't create constructive-dismissal or ERT exposure for the Buyer. Also confirm that the bonuses do not trigger any ESS, FBT or PAYG withholding obligations left with the Company.
- Warranty that there are no other transaction-related payments, retention bonuses, accelerated vesting, or change-of-control entitlements beyond those scheduled.

### 4.4 Ironquay Development Studio (DD-004/DD-010) – SOW3 Project Materials only transfer on cleared payment; AUD 180k open

An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" misses the point. The exposure is not AUD 180k – it is that the Company may not **own the IP in its own product deliverables** until a contractor is paid, and even then the transfer may require a confirmatory assignment. If that IP is embedded in the Paperbark platform, this is a core-asset chain-of-title defect.

**Position:**
- Completion deliverables (or CP): evidence of cleared payment of all SOW1–SOW3 fees; written confirmation from Ironquay that no amounts are outstanding; executed confirmatory deed of assignment of all Project Materials (all SOWs) to the Company; moral rights consents from Ironquay personnel.
- If the fee is unpaid at Completion, deduct AUD 180k (plus any interest/late fees) from price and have the Company pay it from those funds at Completion.
- Specific indemnity for all Losses arising from any failure of the Company to own, or any third-party claim to, IP developed by Ironquay (including re-development, licence fees, lost revenue) – outside the cap and basket, 7 years, or a dedicated cap at not less than a meaningful proportion of price.
- Full IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, all contractors have assigned, open-source compliance), not "settled under the general regime".
- Diligence action: have our team confirm whether DD-010 is the AP ledger and obtain bank confirmation of payment status; identify what SOW3 actually built.

### 4.5 Export/privacy incident (DD-006) – ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address

"Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material" is not a position we can accept, for three reasons:

1. On ~AUD 12m revenue the Company is an APP entity under the Privacy Act 1988. The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme required a reasonable and expeditious assessment within **30 days** of becoming aware of a suspected eligible data breach. The incident predates 22 September; as at today the investigation is still described as "preliminary". The Company may already be out of time, which is itself a compliance breach.
2. The data set (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) is personal information; the post-2024 reforms include a statutory tort for serious invasion of privacy (in force since June 2025), expanded OAIC infringement-notice and civil penalty powers, and penalties of the greater of AUD 50m, 3× benefit, or 30% of turnover for serious interferences.
3. Customer contracts (Bluefen in particular) likely contain breach-notification and security obligations; an unremediated incident can be a termination trigger and will surface in the Bluefen consent process.

**Position:**
- Covenant: Seller to procure that the Company completes the assessment, engages forensic support if needed, makes any required OAIC/individual/customer notifications, and remediates **before Completion**, with the Buyer consulted on the notification decision.
- Updated written disclosure of outcome as a condition or completion deliverable; Buyer termination/price-reduction right if the incident is confirmed as an eligible data breach with material consequences.
- **Specific indemnity**, outside cap/basket/time limits (or with its own cap), for all Losses arising from the incident: investigation and notification costs, regulatory penalties and infringement notices, third-party and customer claims, contract terminations, credit-monitoring/remediation.
- Warranties: compliance with Privacy Act/APPs and contractual security obligations; no other incidents; no regulator correspondence.

### 4.6 Office lease (DD-007) – notification obligation

The Seller is careful to say the material "does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent." We should read the lease ourselves (change-of-control provisions are often in the assignment clause). Whatever it is, the Seller should give the required notification pre-Completion as a completion deliverable, and warrant that no landlord consent is required and the lease is not in default. Check also any bank guarantee/security deposit and whether it is Seller- or Company-funded.

### 4.7 Sandbar supplier renewals (DD-008/DD-011) – 3 × AUD 110,000

Three identical, related renewals totalling AUD 330k, which the Seller asks us to "read together for timing/scope" but will not say whether they are terminable, accrued or necessary. The split structure is worth probing – identical amounts can indicate splitting to stay under an approval or material-contract threshold.

**Position:**
- Determine whether they are (a) accrued/unpaid – then they go into net working capital or are debt-like deductions; (b) new commitments entered pre-Completion – then they are subject to the conduct-of-business covenant (no new contracts > AUD 50k or with term > 12 months without Buyer consent); or (c) necessary for operations and already priced in.
- Warranty that the Company has no commitments to Sandbar or related parties beyond those scheduled, and that no related party of the Seller has any interest in Sandbar.
- Confirm termination rights and whether value would be lost on termination.

### 4.8 Mossvale (DD-009) – restriction on assignment

A share sale is not an assignment, so the Seller's point is probably right – but check the clause for change-of-control or "deemed assignment" language and any most-favoured-customer or exclusivity terms. Warranty that no consent is required under any Material Contract as a result of the transaction except as listed. Lower priority.

### 4.9 Title (DD-012) – share register only

A share register is the Company's own record. Para 10 explicitly notes the Buyer has not completed its own verification; that is the Seller setting up the knowledge/discoverability defence.

**Diligence actions:** ASIC company search and historical extract; PPSR search against the Company and against Harbourglass's shares in it; constitution (pre-emptive rights, transfer restrictions, director approval); chain of title from incorporation (transfers, share certificates, stamping); any shareholders' agreement; Harbourglass board resolutions and authority, and whether Harbourglass's own financiers have security over, or consent rights in respect of, the shares.

**Position:** Absolute warranties on title (legal and beneficial owner, free of all Encumbrances, no options or rights to subscribe, register is complete and accurate), uncapped or capped at price, 7 years, no disclosure permitted against them. Completion deliverables: share transfer forms, share certificates (or indemnity for lost certificates), director/secretary resignations, board minutes approving the transfer and updating the register, bank signatory changes.

### 4.10 Tax – "settled under the general regime" – **reject**

Pre-Completion tax risk is conventionally allocated to the Seller through a separate tax indemnity, not the general warranty cap and basket.

**Position:** Tax indemnity for all pre-Completion tax (income tax, GST, PAYG, super guarantee, payroll tax, FBT), 7-year claim period, capped at price, no basket/de minimis, no disclosure. Tax warranties to the same standard. Confirm NSW duty position (share transfer should not attract duty unless the Company is a landholder; unlikely for an analytics business but confirm). Confirm the Company is not and has never been part of a tax consolidated group with Harbourglass; if it has, require a tax sharing agreement and clear exit payment at Completion.

---

## 5. Structural protections to propose

Given the number of known, unresolved items, we should not rely on indemnities alone against a Seller whose covenant strength we have not assessed.

1. **Retention/escrow:** 10–15% of the price (AUD 2.4–3.6m) held in escrow for 18–24 months, available to satisfy warranty and specific indemnity claims, with a staged release and a hold-back for notified claims.
2. **Specific indemnities** (outside cap/basket/time limits) for: Riverlark, Ironquay IP, closing bonuses and on-costs, DD-006, tax, and any pre-Completion non-compliance identified in the lease or Bluefen/Mossvale contracts.
3. **Conditions precedent:** Bluefen consent (Buyer-waivable); DD-006 assessment completed and any notifications made; no MAC.
4. **Completion deliverables:** Riverlark payoff and releases; Ironquay payment evidence and confirmatory assignment; lease notification; updated share register and ASIC Form 484; resignations.
5. **Price mechanics:** confirm the completion accounts / locked box mechanism actually deducts Riverlark, bonuses (grossed up), any accrued Sandbar amounts and the Ironquay fee as Debt/Transaction Expenses. Request a revised funds flow before responding on price.
6. **Conduct of business covenants** signing to Completion, with Buyer consent for new commitments above a threshold.
7. **Restraint of trade** and non-solicitation from Harbourglass and its principals (not mentioned in the Seller's package at all – worth checking the draft SPA).
8. Consider **W&I insurance** as a tool to bridge the cap gap, understanding that all of §4 will be excluded and must be covered by the above.

---

## 6. Summary of recommendations (priority order)

| # | Issue | Buyer position |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fundamental/title/capacity warranties under general cap & 18 months | Reject. 100% cap, 6–7 years, no disclosure/knowledge qualification |
| 2 | Limitations/exclusive remedy/non-reliance apply to "all Claims" | Reject. Carve out fraud, fundamental, tax, specific indemnities, price adjustment, covenants, non-excludable statutory rights |
| 3 | Cl 8.3 deemed Buyer knowledge (incl. "discoverable") | Delete. Fallback: actual knowledge of named individuals only, no constructive/adviser knowledge |
| 4 | General data room/public register disclosure | Reject. Fair-disclosure standard, frozen indexed data room, specified searches, no disclosure against fundamental/tax/indemnities |
| 5 | Riverlark release post-Completion | Reject. Repay at Completion from proceeds; releases and PPSR discharge as deliverables |
| 6 | Bluefen consent "reasonable endeavours"/deemed satisfied on any written consent | Buyer-waivable CP: unconditional or Buyer-acceptable consent with 11.3 satisfied; best endeavours; termination/price protection |
| 7 | Ironquay indemnity limited to SOW3 fee | Payment + confirmatory assignment as deliverables; uncapped IP indemnity; full IP warranties |
| 8 | Bonuses AUD 420k outside funds flow | Deduct from price grossed up for on-costs; indemnity; warranty of no other transaction payments |
| 9 | DD-006 "not material" | Complete NDB assessment/notify pre-Completion; specific indemnity outside limits; privacy warranties |
| 10 | Tax "settled under general regime" | Separate tax indemnity, 7 years, no basket, no disclosure |
| 11 | Cap 20% / de minimis 25k / deductible basket / 18 months | Cap 30–35%+; de minimis AUD 10–15k with aggregation; tipping basket; 24 months general |
| 12 | Sandbar renewals | Classify as accrued/debt-like or subject to conduct covenants; related-party warranty |
| 13 | Lease, Mossvale, title | Buyer to read primary documents; notification as deliverable; consent warranties; full title diligence (ASIC/PPSR/constitution) |
| 14 | Disclosure letter stale (22 Sept) | Bring-down at Completion; supplementary disclosure doesn't cure; termination right for material new matters |
| 15 | Overall | Escrow 10–15%; revised funds flow before responding on price; check restraints in SPA; consider W&I for residual |

If useful, I can turn this into a mark-up table against the Seller's clause references for the formal response, or draft the specific indemnity and CP language for Riverlark, Bluefen, Ironquay and DD-006.
